heading: Consequence: no multi-pattern rules
text:
### Consequence: no multi-pattern rules [LNOG.6.2]

Under `logical: false`, logical-lifecycle schemas are banned (LNOG.3.1).
Therefore LNLS.3.3 can never be satisfied for any multi-pattern rule.
Any multi-pattern rule in a program with `linear_scan: false` and
`logical: false` is a compile error: LNLS.3.3 fires because no
logical-schema identity anchor exists.

Effectively, the two settings together imply **single-pattern rules
only** — every rule's LHS references exactly one schema pattern.  The
beta network is absent.  Every operation is an alpha-level operation:

| Operation | Cost |
|---|---|
| Assert | O(1): working-memory insert, alpha lookup, agenda insert |
| Retract | O(1): working-memory remove, alpha-memory remove; no beta, no TMS |
| Rule firing | per activation, linear in its rule's actions and their expressions |
| TTL tick (default) | O(expired × log n_ttl_schemas + n_ttl_schemas) ([LDTL.6.1]) |

With `dynamic_ttl: false`, no cost per fact grows with the number of live
facts, and none has a beta or TMS term. This is the **alpha-only operating
mode**. Under `dynamic_ttl: true`, an assert and the TTL tick each gain the
deadline heap's O(log N_ttl) term ([LCAP.2.4]).
